references.text: God separates the land of Goshen where the Israelites live, so that the flies do not come there. This shows the same pattern of God's protection over His people.
God makes a distinction between the livestock of the Israelites and the livestock of the Egyptians during the plague. The same principle of God's protection of Israel.
During the plague of darkness, all the Israelites had light where they lived, while Egypt was in darkness. This shows the same pattern with an exception for God's people.
God makes a distinction between the Egyptians and Israel during the final plague. Continuation of the theme of God's protection.
The blood on the doorposts protects the Israelites from the angel of death. God's people are spared from judgment over Egypt.
Joseph tells that the family should live in the land of Goshen. The first time Goshen is mentioned as the Israelites' dwelling place in Egypt.
Goshen is given to Jacob's family as their dwelling place in Egypt.
Israel settled in the land of Goshen and became fruitful there. Background for why the Israelites were in Goshen.
